prerequisites: linear differential equations is advantageous but not essential

learning_outcomes.text: Students are acquainted with principles of automatic control presented by means of examples of processes and devices the students are familiar with.
Students get informative understanding of the nature of the solved control problems.
Students get knowledge of notions used in control system theory and real practice in usage of MATLAB/Simulink software.
Obtained skills can be applied without the control in computation and dynamic simulation of technological processes.

syllabus_topics: Principles of automatic control, terminology, tasks.
Control system as a tool for designing, modelling, investigating real control circuits.
Controlled processes, description, modelling, ways of control.
Controller selection and its parameter setting from the viewpoint stability and control quality.
Controllers operating continuously and discreetly in time - comparison, special features.
All demonstrated by examples continuously processed in MATLAB/Simulink program.
teaching_methods: Own solving problems by means program Matlab/Simulink
assessment_rules: It will be possible to demonstrate these problems in a project as another subject assessed up to 5 credits.
bibliography: Seborg, D., Edgar, T., Mellichamp, D.: Process Dynamics and Control. John Wiley Sons, New York, Chichester, Brisbane, Toronto, Singapore 1989. ISBN 0-471-86389-0
Ogata, K.: Modern Control Engineering. 4th Ed., Prentice Hall, 2002. ISBN 0-13-060907-2
